A default text logical model is set

steps.title: Configure products, points, and payments
steps.description: Create sellable plans or points products, verify model pricing, then enable payment channels according to actual merchant credentials.
checks: At least one product is enabled
Model base points have a clear rule
Payment callback URL matches the site's HTTPS domain

steps.title: Decide storage and recovery plan
steps.description: Choose local media or S3-compatible storage, and decide how to back up and restore both PostgreSQL and media files.
checks: Media write test succeeds
Data directory or bucket is persisted
A reproducible recovery drill has been completed
Permissions for administrators, regular users, and banned users behave as expected
Text, image, and video each complete one real call for every enabled capability
Ordering, payment, points crediting, failure refunds, and media reads all have verification records
warnings: Do not open public registration or charge users before models, storage, and payments are verified.
The database, media, and encryption key must be managed as one recovery asset set; missing any one of them means it is not recoverable.

links.label: Initial setup
links.description: View go-live readiness progress and the next configuration item

links.label: Data backup
links.description: Export, restore, and verify backup boundaries

stepActions: In the install wizard, first test the PostgreSQL host, port, database name, and account permissions; initialize the schema only after the test passes.
After creating the first administrator, log out and log back in once to confirm auth, sessions, and admin routes all recover normally.
Upload the JoveCanvas Logo in site profile, and check the login page, user app, admin, favicon, and assistant avatar for any triangle-brand fallback.
Add a working text channel in model channels, pull models, then create a logical model, enable the binding, set it as default, and run one real text check.
First create an internal test product with a clear price, points or plan entitlement, and validity period, then verify the base points of the corresponding logical model.
Enable only one payment channel whose merchant credentials, keys, and HTTPS callback are fully verified, and run a small test order through payment and entitlement crediting.
After choosing local or S3, upload one image and one short video, refresh the page to confirm they still load, and record each one's storage_provider.
Back up PostgreSQL, the media directory or bucket, environment variables, and the encryption key separately, and complete one recovery verification in an isolated environment.

troubleshooting.symptom: Code has changed, but port 3000 still shows the old page or still redirects to GitHub
troubleshooting.cause: Port 3000 is still running an old `next start` production build, or the reverse proxy still points to an old container, old port, or old static directory.
actions: Check which process listens on 3000 and its start command; use `npm run dev` during development.
In production mode rebuild and restart the current instance, then confirm the proxy target and browser cache.
troubleshooting.caution: Changing source code alone will not update an already-running production build; do not let multiple project instances compete for the same port.

troubleshooting.symptom: The administrator can log in, but Agent, image, or video calls fail immediately
troubleshooting.cause: The default logical model is not set, no binding is enabled, or the upstream Base URL, API Key, protocol, and model type don't match.
actions: Test the default text logical model first, then test image and video capabilities separately.
In call records, verify the logical model, the real upstream model, the request URL, and the first error.

troubleshooting.symptom: The payment page accepts orders, but no points or plan arrive after successful payment
troubleshooting.cause: The payment callback never arrived, signature verification failed, the order number doesn't match, or callback handling didn't complete idempotent entitlement granting.
actions: Verify the public HTTPS callback URL, merchant keys, and channel event records.
Confirm the callback status in orders and financial ledger before deciding on compensation; do not edit balances directly first.

operations.title: Dashboard, users, and generation operations
operations.summary: View platform trends, manage user entitlements, and locate generation task and upstream call issues.
operations.purpose: Use the summary to judge whether the platform is healthy, then drill down layer by layer through users, tasks, and call records; don't judge business health from a single success rate or request volume.

steps.title: Start with the dashboard
steps.description: Watch for abnormal changes in active users, revenue, points liability, request trends, success rate, and model distribution.
checks: The statistics time range is explicit
Revenue and order metrics use the same definition
Abnormal spikes can be located to a date and model

steps.title: Verify permissions and entitlements per user
steps.description: In user operations, view account status, roles, plans, and points; confirm the business reason before any manual adjustment.
checks: Administrator roles were not changed by mistake
Plan and points adjustments have a clear reason
Banned users cannot create new tasks

steps.title: Locate a single request in call records
steps.description: Filter by user, type, source, status, and time to view model, duration, errors, and related media.
checks: Logical model and real upstream model confirmed
Creation failures and query failures are distinguished
Whether a failure has been refunded is verified

steps.title: Handle tasks in generation operations
steps.description: View tasks, sessions, projects, channel health, and points costs in one place; only recreate an upstream task when the user explicitly retries.
checks: No duplicate upstream tasks of the same kind were created
Failure records remain auditable
Cancel, timeout, and refund states are consistent
Business metrics can drill down to real orders or tasks
No obvious mismatch between user permissions, plans, and balances
Failed tasks have an error, a refund, and a user-visible status
warnings: Do not delete records still needed for auditing, refunds, or media references just to clean up the list.
Manually adding points changes financial liability; keep the reason and reconcile the ledger at the same time.

links.label: Call records
links.description: View details of a single generation

stepActions: Always review both the last 24 hours and the last 7 days, and compare users, revenue, request volume, and success rate with the previous period.
After spotting a spike or cliff, record the exact time, then drill down by model, task type, and entry point.
Search for the target user, first verify account status and role, then review plan validity, remaining quota, points balance, and recent ledger entries.
When manually adjusting entitlements, fill in the business reason, then verify with a fresh regular session that permissions take effect immediately.
Narrow records by user, time, and task type, then open a single call to view the logical model, upstream model, task ID, duration, and error.
Handle creation failures, polling failures, timeouts, and upstream terminal failures separately, and verify the corresponding consumption ledger entry was reversed.
From an abnormal task, enter the related session, project, and media to confirm the front-end display state matches the server-side task terminal state.
When a retry is needed, have the user trigger it explicitly: clear old subtask state first, then create a new upstream request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The dashboard shows 0, but users, orders, or tasks actually exist
troubleshooting.cause: The statistics time range, database provider, timezone, or aggregation query doesn't match the currently running instance.
actions: Confirm the page time range and server timezone.
Verify the data source with the raw lists of orders, users, or call records, then check which database the current instance is connected to.

troubleshooting.symptom: One generation request produced multiple upstream tasks or duplicate charges
troubleshooting.cause: The page was submitted repeatedly, a recovery flow created the task again, or the server lacks a stable idempotency key.
actions: Compare duplicate records by user, session, Run, and upstream task ID.
Keep failure evidence and stop automatic recreation; start a new task only on explicit user retry.
troubleshooting.caution: Do not delete duplicate records to hide the problem; reconcile points, plan quota, and upstream costs first.

troubleshooting.symptom: A user has been banned, but old pages are still visible or old tasks keep running
troubleshooting.cause: The user kept an old session, or the ban happened after the task was already submitted.
actions: Have the user re-request a protected endpoint and confirm server-side auth rejects it.
Distinguish blocking new tasks from terminating existing upstream tasks, and handle incurred costs and results per business rules.

commerce.title: Plans, promotions, coupons, referrals, and orders
commerce.summary: Configure real regular and campaign prices, manage coupons and referral rewards, and handle payment and after-sales from the order snapshot.
commerce.purpose: Show users real, explainable discounts, build revocable single-level referral growth, and ensure orders are unaffected by later product, promotion, or coupon changes once created.

steps.title: Create products and regular prices first
steps.description: Set the product name, price, points or plan entitlement, validity period, and display status; the regular price must be a real sellable price.
checks: Price unit and entitlement quantities are correct
Product enable/disable matches the launch plan
Purchasing grants the corresponding points or plan

steps.title: Configure limited-time promotions
steps.description: For products that already have a regular price, set the campaign period, campaign label, and campaign price; a product must not have overlapping campaigns.
checks: Campaign price is below the real regular price
Start and end times are correct
The front-end shows the strikethrough only when conditions are met

steps.title: Create and issue coupons
steps.description: Configure fixed-amount or percentage discounts, applicable products, thresholds, validity, stock, and per-user limits, then decide between self-claim or targeted distribution.
checks: Discount scope doesn't conflict with campaign rules
Stock and per-user limits are reasonable
For issued templates, only change the description, toggle, and total quantity that are allowed to change

steps.title: Configure referral rewards
steps.description: In marketing, set inviter points, new-user points or coupons, minimum first-order payment, cooling-off period, monthly/campaign caps, and risk-freeze policy, then enable the program.
checks: Rewards and thresholds match the acquisition-cost budget
Coupon validity covers the expected settlement time
The maintenance task and manual settlement entry are available

steps.title: Handle after-sales from the order snapshot
steps.description: Verify the regular price, campaign discount, coupon discount, and amount actually paid, then perform manual confirmation, closure, or full-order refund.
checks: Paid amount matches the order's amount due
Coupons locked by pending orders are released after cancellation or timeout
Post-refund entitlement and coupon states follow the rules
Front-end price, checkout page, and order detail amounts are consistent
Display is correct before and after campaign boundary times
Coupon claim, lock, release, redemption, and refund flows are traceable
Referral registration, first order, pending settlement, granted, and revoked metrics can be distinguished
warnings: Never fabricate an original price to create a strikethrough; a discount may be shown only when the real regular price is higher than the current price.
After an order is created, only the price and rule snapshot saved with the order may be used; do not recalculate against current campaigns.
Referral rewards support only a single-level relationship; a single network signal may trigger review or freezing, but cannot by itself be treated as fraud.

links.label: Promotions
links.description: Manage campaign periods and campaign prices

links.label: Coupons
links.description: Create templates and distribute to users

links.label: Referral rewards
links.description: Configure first-order rewards, cooling-off, and risk control

stepActions: When creating a product, fill in the name, real regular price, points or plan entitlement, validity, and sort order item by item; keep it disabled until internal checks are done.
After enabling, verify the name, price, entitlements, and description on the plans page, checkout page, and order preview.
Select the target product, set the campaign start and end times, campaign label, and campaign price, and check for overlapping campaigns on the same product before saving.
Verify the selling price before, during, and after the campaign; show the strikethrough only when the campaign price is below the real regular price.
Decide fixed-amount or percentage discount first, then configure the threshold, applicable products, validity, stock, and per-user claim limit.
Use three test accounts — eligible, ineligible, and at the limit — to verify claiming, using, locking, and releasing.
Set inviter and new-user rewards based on acquisition cost first, then configure the minimum first-order payment, cooling-off period, monthly/campaign caps, and auto-freeze policy.

After enabling, use multiple test accounts to verify referral visits, registration binding, first-order triggering, settlement at maturity, refund revocation, and manual recovery, and confirm the maintenance schedule is configured.
Open the order detail and verify the regular price, campaign discount, coupon discount, amount paid, and entitlement snapshot.
Before closing, manually confirming, or refunding, check the payment channel status; after processing, re-check coupons, points, plan, and ledger.

troubleshooting.symptom: The front-end doesn't show the discount strikethrough or campaign price
troubleshooting.cause: The campaign is not enabled, the time hasn't taken effect, the campaign price is not below the regular price, or the product is not in the campaign scope.
actions: Verify the server time, campaign start/end times, and product binding.
Compare the product's regular price with the current transaction price, and refresh the plans and checkout pages to confirm.
troubleshooting.caution: Do not temporarily raise the regular price just to show a strikethrough; the original price must be a long-term real sellable price.

troubleshooting.symptom: A user clearly claimed a coupon, but it's unavailable at checkout
troubleshooting.cause: The threshold isn't met, the product isn't applicable, it's expired, stock or the user's claim count is exhausted, or the coupon is locked by another pending order.
actions: In coupon records, verify the status, applicable scope, and locking order.
Cancel the old order or wait for it to time out, confirm the lock is released, then check out again.

troubleshooting.symptom: After a refund, the amount, coupon, and user entitlements don't add up
troubleshooting.cause: Only the order status was updated; the payment refund, entitlement revocation, or coupon status is not yet complete.
actions: Reconcile against the price and discount snapshot saved when the order was created.
Check in turn the payment refund ledger, points or plan revocation, and coupon refund rules.

troubleshooting.symptom: An invited user has paid, but the reward wasn't granted
troubleshooting.cause: The order isn't the first paid order, the amount is below the threshold, it's still in the cooling-off period, the relationship is risk-frozen, the reward quota is exhausted, or the maintenance settlement task hasn't run yet.
actions: In referral relationships and reward records, verify the triggering order, risk status, settlement time, and rejection reason.
Confirm the order's terminal state and the maintenance schedule before using settle-now; do not bypass the reward ledger by manually adding points.
troubleshooting.caution: Before restoring a frozen relationship, the review basis must be recorded; when a locked or redeemed reward coupon is refunded, it must be handled manually — do not fake a successful revocation.

finance.title: Points, payment channels, CDKs, and financial ledger
finance.summary: Reconcile model pricing, payment configuration, redemption codes, and fund/points ledger in one place.
finance.purpose: Ensure every purchase, generation, refund, or redemption can be cross-checked across orders, payment ledger, points ledger, and plan usage.

steps.title: Establish unified points rules
steps.description: Configure base points per logical model, and set parameter multipliers such as image count, video duration, and resolution.
checks: The user's estimated points and the server's actual charge use the same rule
Free calls also record idempotent ledger entries and plan quota usage
Failed tasks can reverse points and plan usage

steps.title: Configure and test payment channels
steps.description: Enable only channels that have merchant credentials, keys, certificates, and an HTTPS callback, and complete a test payment for each.
checks: Callback signature verification passes
Duplicate and out-of-order events don't grant entitlements twice
Refunds write back to orders and ledger

steps.title: Issue and track CDKs
steps.description: Generate points or plan redemption codes for campaigns or after-sales scenarios, with usage count, validity, and notes; export plaintext only once at generation time.
checks: Distribution scope and quantity are traceable
Expired or disabled codes cannot be redeemed
Redeeming user and time can be verified

steps.title: Reconcile the financial ledger daily
steps.description: Compare orders, actual channel receipts, refunds, points liability, and abnormal reconciliation items; keep evidence first when a discrepancy is found.
checks: Paid orders have a successful payment ledger entry
Refunded orders' refund ledger and entitlement states are consistent
Manual adjustments have a note and a responsible person
Payment callbacks have idempotency evidence
Points balance matches the ledger sum
Order amount, actual payment received, and refund amount can be cross-checked
warnings: API Keys, private keys, certificates, and webhook secrets may only be stored in server-side configuration or environment variables.
Do not fix accounting by editing the database directly; use the existing business entries and keep an audit trail.

links.label: Points rules
links.description: Configure model pricing and parameter multipliers

stepActions: Configure base points by logical model ID first, then configure parameter multipliers such as count, duration, and resolution item by item.
Run once each with a free model, a regular model, and high-multiplier parameters, and compare the front-end estimate, consumption ledger, and failure reversal.
For each payment channel, fill in the server-side keys, certificates, callback URL, and required environment variables, then run the configuration check after saving.
Use test or small-amount orders to verify creation, payment, duplicate callbacks, out-of-order callbacks, and refunds — don't just verify the redirect page.
Create CDKs by campaign batch, recording purpose, entitlement, quantity, validity, and owner, and export the plaintext in a controlled way immediately after generation.
Verify redemption results and the points or plan ledger with codes in four states: unused, used, expired, and disabled.
Each day, compare successful orders, actual receipts, refunds, and fees per channel, then reconcile points balance, plan quota, and manual adjustments.
When a discrepancy is found, record the order number, channel transaction number, and consumption ledger ID; freeze duplicate processing first, then locate the cause.

troubleshooting.symptom: The front-end estimated points don't match the actual charge
troubleshooting.cause: The front-end prices by logical model while the server prices by upstream alias, or parameter multipliers don't use the same resolution rule.
actions: In call records, confirm the logical model ID, upstream model, and resolved pointsCost.
Always read from the logical model pricing rule; for free calls, also check plan quota and idempotent ledger entries.

troubleshooting.symptom: A user received duplicate entitlements after a payment channel's repeated callbacks
troubleshooting.cause: Callback events or order entitlement granting lack idempotency constraints, so repeated events were treated as new payments.
actions: Check for duplicate records by channel event ID, order number, and payment ledger.
Pause manual re-granting, fix the idempotency state first, then reverse the extra entitlements with an audit trail.

troubleshooting.symptom: A CDK can't be redeemed, or its plaintext can't be found in the admin console
troubleshooting.cause: The code is expired, disabled, or has reached its usage limit, and the system stores only a secure digest, not the plaintext long-term.
actions: Check redemption records by batch, status, and notes.
If the plaintext is lost, generate a new batch and disable the old one; do not try to recover it from the database.

models.title: Model channels, logical models, and Agent Skills
models.summary: Wrap real upstream models into stable logical capabilities, and configure executable professional Skills for the Agent.
models.purpose: Let regular users choose only stable product capabilities, while the server handles upstream channels, model aliases, priority, and failover — keeping keys and vendor details away from the browser.

steps.title: Add and test upstream channels
steps.description: Follow the six-step wizard to pick a protocol, configure the connection, fetch models, verify capabilities, bind logical models, and review before enabling; for unknown upstreams, use the custom protocol assistant to generate a reviewable draft.
checks: SD2 and Stable Diffusion protocols are not mixed up
Base URL doesn't contain incorrect duplicated path segments
Auth-free protocols don't force an API Key
Capability checks use a real callable model
Keys are never returned to the regular user side

steps.title: Create logical models and bindings
steps.description: Set name, type, and enable state for user-facing capabilities, then bind channels, real models, and priority.
checks: Logical model type matches the upstream capability
At least one enabled binding is available
The base points key uses the logical model ID

steps.title: Set system default models
steps.description: The default text model serves the workbench Agent, Canvas planning, internal analysis, and creation review — verify it first.
checks: The default text model responds reliably
Image, video, and audio defaults point to the corresponding capabilities
Disabled channels are no longer selected

steps.title: Configure Agent Skills
steps.description: Set name, category, trigger words, capability constraints, and execution rules for professional capabilities, keeping each Skill matched to real available models.
checks: Trigger descriptions are clear and don't conflict
Skills don't include capabilities unavailable to users
After enable/disable, the user-side selection state is correct
Text, image, video, and audio are each tested within their enabled scope
Default logical models, bound channels, and billing rules are consistent
Internal text tasks of Agent and Canvas explicitly carry a logical model ID
warnings: Custom protocol analysis results are only channel-level drafts and must be reviewed and tested before enabling; there is currently no global protocol version publish/rollback.
Do not use the real upstream model name as a long-term pricing key; after a channel change, front-end estimates and server charges will diverge.
When testing keys, don't copy full requests, responses, or keys into announcements, docs, or browser logs.

links.label: Model channels
links.description: Configure channels, models, and default capabilities

links.label: Agent Skills
links.description: Manage professional capabilities and trigger rules

stepActions: In model channels, follow the wizard to pick a protocol, configure the connection, pull models, verify capabilities, bind logical models, and review before enabling; auth-free protocols don't need an API Key.
For unknown upstreams, use the custom protocol assistant to import docs or examples, review the request path, auth, templates, and result fields, then run a real check.
Create a stable logical model ID for each user-visible capability, set its type and display name, then add one or more channel bindings with priority.
Disable and enable bindings one by one to verify routing order, and confirm that when no binding is available the server fails explicitly instead of silently switching types.
Set and verify the default text model first, because admin planning, Agent, Canvas, and internal analysis all depend on it.
Then set the image, video, and audio default capabilities, and verify as a regular user that page selections match actual routing.
Write clear trigger scope, input limits, and output goals for each Skill, and bind it to a real enabled logical capability.
Test once with a similar request and once with an unrelated request, confirming it neither misfires nor shows an executable state when unavailable to the user.

troubleshooting.symptom: Channel checks return 404, path not found, or protocol errors
troubleshooting.cause: The Base URL already contains /v1 but the request template appends it again, or the selected protocol doesn't match the vendor's API format.
actions: Check the base address and final request path against the vendor's documentation.
Switch to the correct protocol supported by the project and re-pull models; don't trial-and-error by concatenating paths.

troubleshooting.symptom: The model list can be pulled, but real calls still fail
troubleshooting.cause: The account lacks permission for that model, the model type is wrong, the binding isn't enabled, or the model supports only some parameters.
actions: Use the channel check to send a minimal request to the target model.
Read the upstream status code and response summary in call records, then adjust bindings and parameters.

troubleshooting.symptom: Agent text works, but image or video is never available
troubleshooting.cause: Only the default text model was verified; the image or video logical model has no available binding, default value, or corresponding billing rule.
actions: Run image and video capability checks separately.
Confirm the logical type, default model, upstream binding, and points rule all use the same logical model ID.

system.title: Site profile, basic settings, and user rights
system.summary: Manage branding, registration and email, generation defaults, account deletion, and version information in one place.
system.purpose: Keep branding consistent across public pages, the user workspace, and the admin console, and give registration, email, default generation settings, and user-rights handling clear operational boundaries.

steps.title: Maintain site profile and branding
steps.description: Set the site name, SEO, social links, homepage content, and JoveCanvas Logo; the browser icon and assistant avatar use the same brand source.
checks: Logo, ICO, favicon, and admin identity are consistent
Neither the default nor the fallback icon is the triangle brand
Clear and readable on both light and dark backgrounds

steps.title: Configure registration, SMTP, and generation defaults
steps.description: Test SMTP first, then enable email-dependent registration, recovery, and re-binding flows; set generation default parameters according to real model capabilities.
checks: The test email arrives successfully
Registration policy matches the operations plan
Default parameters don't exceed what the upstream supports

steps.title: Handle deletion requests
steps.description: Verify the applicant's identity, business records, and retention obligations, record the accept/reject reason, and handle public content and personal data per the rules.
checks: Request status and notes are complete
Financial and audit data are retained per policy
Public content and media permissions are updated in sync

steps.title: Review version and upgrade information
steps.description: Before upgrading, read the version changes and deployment requirements, back up the database and media, then update per the release process.
checks: Current and target versions are explicit
The pre-upgrade backup is restorable
Core pages and capabilities are regression-tested after the upgrade
All brand entry points use the JoveCanvas Logo
Registration, verification codes, and password recovery flows match the SMTP state
Deletion and upgrade operations both have traceable records
warnings: After changing the Logo, also check favicon, manifest, metadata, login page, user app, admin, and assistant avatar.
Before enabling email registration, a real inbox test must pass, or users won't be able to log in or recover passwords.

links.label: Site profile
links.description: Manage branding, SEO, and homepage content

links.label: Basic settings
links.description: Manage registration, email, and generation defaults

stepActions: Upload the JoveCanvas Logo in site profile, then after saving check the homepage, login, user workspace, admin, assistant avatar, and browser icon in turn.
Also check light mode, dark mode, favicon, manifest, and metadata fallbacks to make sure no default state shows the triangle brand mark.
Save the SMTP host, port, SSL, account, authorization code, and sender first, and send a real test email.
Enable registration or recovery flows only after email verification passes; set generation default parameters within the range supported by the current default logical model.
Open the deletion request and verify user identity, request time, public content, media, orders, and audit retention requirements.
Record the accept or reject reason, then after execution verify account status, public content, and media permissions through regular endpoints.
In the update center, confirm the current version, changelog, and upgrade requirements, and back up the database and media first.
After upgrading, check install status, login, generation, payment, storage, and the admin docs before deciding whether to open traffic.

troubleshooting.symptom: The JoveCanvas Logo was uploaded, but some pages still show the old icon or a triangle
troubleshooting.cause: The admin configuration, /logo.svg, /icon.svg, favicon, manifest, metadata, or assistant avatar still has independent hardcoding, plus browser cache.
actions: Check each brand source and the actual request URLs one by one.
Clean old builds and restart, hard-refresh the browser, then verify light mode, dark mode, and logged-out state.
troubleshooting.caution: Functional triangle icons such as play or alert may be kept, but must not be used as the brand Logo, default placeholder, or fallback.

troubleshooting.symptom: The SMTP test succeeds, but users don't receive verification or recovery emails
troubleshooting.cause: The business toggle isn't enabled, the sender doesn't match the authenticated account, mail lands in spam, or a sending rate limit is triggered.
actions: Check the registration policy, email task errors, and the target mailbox's spam folder.
Verify the From address, DNS records, and SMTP provider limits, then retest with different mailboxes.

troubleshooting.symptom: Light mode looks fine, but after switching to dark mode text, buttons, or icons become unreadable
troubleshooting.cause: The component only set the background, without explicitly setting dark-mode text, border, hover, or icon colors.
actions: Check all clickable states of the component and Ant Design Portal overlays.
Provide readable contrast separately for light, dark, hover, active, and disabled states.

storage.title: Local media, external storage, and data backup
storage.summary: Manage where media is actually stored, historical providers, reference protection, migration, and recovery boundaries.
storage.purpose: Ensure new media has a clear write location, historical media always stays readable, deletion never breaks business references, and the database and media can be recovered as a set.

steps.title: Inspect local media
steps.description: View server media by type, source, user, and retention period; before deleting, confirm references from creative sessions, assets, Canvas, dramas, and generation records.
checks: Media records user ownership and source
Temporary and permanent file boundaries are clear
Referenced files cannot be force-deleted

steps.title: Configure S3-compatible storage
steps.description: Fill in Endpoint, Region, Bucket, credentials, object prefix, and path-style; enable only after the connection test succeeds.
checks: Upload, read, and delete permissions follow least privilege
External access uses short-lived signed URLs
Business records store only the stable storageKey

steps.title: Migrate historical media
steps.description: Migrate in batches and verify object upload, registration, and in-site reads item by item; delete local source files only after confirming external objects are usable.
checks: Migration tasks are retryable and don't double-register
Historical records are still read via their original storage_provider
The current toggle doesn't change where historical media lives

steps.title: Establish complete backups
steps.description: Business data export cannot replace database and media backups; production recovery must cover PostgreSQL, media or bucket, configuration, and the encryption key together.
checks: Backup files are desensitized and stored under control
Recovery steps have a clear order
Sample restores or full drills are performed regularly
Both local and external media can be read via their registered provider
Referenced media cannot be deleted by admin cleanup by mistake
The recovery environment can re-read users, tasks, and media
warnings: The external storage toggle only decides where new media is written; it cannot be used to switch where historical media is read from.
Do not use force to bypass media reference protection; a file deleted while business records still point to it is a data incident.

links.label: Local media
links.description: View files, retention periods, and references

stepActions: Filter local media by user, source, type, and time, then open the detail to confirm the original filename, ownership, and business associations.
Before deleting, review the reference check results; if sessions, assets, Canvas, dramas, or tasks reference it, resolve the business relationship first.
Fill in Endpoint, Region, Bucket, access credentials, object prefix, and path-style, and run the connection test with a least-privilege account.
After enabling, upload new media, confirm it's registered as the external provider in the database, and that in-site reads use short-lived signed URLs.
Migrate a small batch of historical media first, verifying object upload, registration, in-site reads, and the original business pages.
Migrate in batches only after confirming the target objects are stably readable, and keep the failure list for idempotent retries.
Make a same-batch backup plan covering PostgreSQL, media, configuration, and the encryption key, recording the version and creator.
Restore in an isolated environment per the docs, spot-check users, tasks, local media, and external objects, and record recovery time and gaps.

troubleshooting.symptom: After switching to external storage, historical images or videos suddenly won't open
troubleshooting.cause: The read logic incorrectly follows the current storage toggle instead of reading via each media record's registered storage_provider.
actions: Inspect the failing media's provider, storageKey, and registration record.
Restore reading by historical provider; the storage toggle only affects new writes from then on.

troubleshooting.symptom: S3 connection or upload succeeds, but user pages still can't display the media
troubleshooting.cause: The signed URL, public/private Endpoint choice, server time, object permissions, or response Content-Type is incorrect.
actions: Get a fresh signed URL from the in-site media API and check the status code.
Verify server time, object key, signature validity, and minimal read permission.

troubleshooting.symptom: The admin console says the media is referenced and can't be deleted
troubleshooting.cause: The file is still associated with creative sessions, the asset library, Canvas, dramas, or generation records — reference protection is working.
actions: Follow the reference list into the corresponding business records to confirm whether they can be unlinked.
Take down or delete the business entities first, then delete the media again.
troubleshooting.caution: Do not use force to bypass reference protection, or you'll get a data incident where records are visible but the file won't open.

content.title: Announcements and public prompt operations
content.summary: Publish in-site notifications and public creation assets while controlling reach, content quality, and takedown cadence.
content.purpose: Use announcements to convey necessary information and public prompts to lower the creation barrier; both should serve real operational goals — avoid unrestrained popups and piles of low-quality content.

steps.title: Create and preview announcements
steps.description: Write a clear title and body, decide whether to enable it and whether it pops up on the homepage or after login, then check reading length on mobile.
checks: Publish time and reach scope are correct
Important links open
Popups don't block users from logging in or creating

steps.title: Control the announcement lifecycle
steps.description: Take down old announcements promptly after campaigns end, incidents recover, or rules expire, so users don't keep acting on outdated information.
checks: Pinned content is still valid
Duplicate announcements are merged
After takedown, users no longer see the popup

steps.title: Maintain public prompts
steps.description: Configure title, body, category, tags, cover, and preview for reusable prompts, and confirm they execute in the target model or workbench.
checks: Prompts contain no keys or internal planning
Categories and tags are searchable
Example results match the description
Announcements and prompts show only enabled content
Titles, bodies, and buttons don't overflow on mobile
Content doesn't leak user data, upstream keys, or the platform's internal prompts
warnings: Post-login popups should be used only for genuinely necessary information; frequent interruptions reduce users' likelihood of finishing creations and paying.
Public prompts should pass content-safety and real-model availability checks before publishing.

links.label: Announcements
links.description: Create, edit, and take down announcements

stepActions: Decide the announcement's goal and audience first, create a draft with a short title, clear body, and necessary links, then check desktop and mobile previews.
Enable homepage or post-login popups only for incidents, rules, or important campaigns, and verify as a regular user after saving.
Record start, end, or takedown conditions for each announcement, and regularly check whether pinned and popup content is still valid.
Disable promptly after the event ends; when copy needs fixing, prefer updating the same announcement to avoid duplicate reach.
For public prompts, fill in a searchable title, complete body, category, tags, and preview, and run them on the corresponding real model first.
Confirm they contain no API Keys, internal planning prompts, or user privacy before enabling, and periodically take down stale content.

troubleshooting.symptom: A user sees the same announcement repeatedly on every login
troubleshooting.cause: The announcement keeps the post-login popup enabled, or the user's acknowledgment state, announcement version, and identity association aren't saved correctly.
actions: Confirm whether the announcement still needs forced reach.
Check user acknowledgment records and the announcement version; disable expired content directly instead of stacking new announcements to fix it.

troubleshooting.symptom: A prompt tests fine in the admin console, but users can't find it or it fails to execute
troubleshooting.cause: The prompt isn't enabled, the category filter doesn't match, or the example uses a model capability not enabled on the user side.
actions: Check enable state, category, and search keywords as a regular user.
Re-run on a logical model users can actually select, and fix the copy and preview.

troubleshooting.symptom: Announcements or prompts scroll horizontally on mobile and buttons get cut off
troubleshooting.cause: The body contains very long URLs, fixed widths, desktop card padding, or non-wrapping text.
actions: Check the page and inner scroll containers at 390px and 430px.
Make long links and body text wrap, use compact spacing on mobile, and shorten action copy.

maintenance.title: Daily inspection and troubleshooting
maintenance.summary: Check users, tasks, channels, accounting, storage, and versions in a fixed order to narrow down failures quickly.
maintenance.purpose: Judge the blast radius and data consistency first, then locate the single user, task, channel, or infrastructure piece — avoid repeatedly changing configuration without enough evidence.

steps.title: Confirm the blast radius
steps.description: Determine whether all users, one capability class, one channel, or a single task is affected, and record the start time and reproducible steps.
checks: Whether login and normal pages work
Whether text, image, and video fail at the same time
Whether only new tasks or historical media are affected

steps.title: Check tasks and channels
steps.description: From generation operations, enter call records and verify the logical model, upstream model, request status, error, duration, and channel check.
checks: Only one upstream task was created
Polling queries the same task ID
Failure refunds and plan quota reversals are correct

steps.title: Check accounting and storage
steps.description: For generation failures reconcile the points ledger; for payment failures reconcile orders and payment ledger; for media failures verify storage_provider, objects, or local files.
checks: No duplicate charges or entitlement grants
Refunds don't depend on the page being opened again
Media URLs don't leak object keys or permanent upstream addresses

steps.title: Post-recovery review
steps.description: Verify the user main flow, record the root cause, fix, affected data, and preventive items; when data is involved, back up before any batch processing.
checks: Functionality recovered on desktop and mobile
Historical tasks and media are still readable
Similar incidents have tests, alerts, or documentation as prevention
Incident timeline, blast radius, and evidence are complete
Final states of tasks, accounting, and media are consistent
At least one real user-path verification is completed after recovery
warnings: Do not delete failure records to make the success rate look normal; they are the basis for refunds, auditing, and review.
Without database, media, and configuration backups, do not perform batch fixes, migrations, or upgrades.

links.label: Data backup
links.description: Save a restore point before batch operations

stepActions: Record the incident start time, affected users, entry points, and capability types, then reproduce with one administrator and one regular user.
Check login and static pages first, separating site-wide failures, single-capability failures, single-channel failures, and single-task failures.
Find the abnormal task by time in generation operations, then enter call records to view the logical model, upstream model, task ID, status, and first error.
Run the channel check and verify each subtask was created only once; don't keep switching models and retrying before the cause is known.
For generation issues reconcile consumption and refund ledger; for payment issues reconcile orders and channel events; for media issues verify provider, storageKey, and the real object.
When states are inconsistent, export evidence and back up first, then fix through business entries instead of editing the database directly.
After recovery, regression-test desktop and mobile in the order: login, text, image, video, payment, media, historical records.
Record root cause, affected data, fix, and preventive measures; add tests, alerts, or inspection items for automatically detectable problems.

troubleshooting.symptom: After changing a model or channel, all new generation tasks fail at once
troubleshooting.cause: The default logical model, enabled bindings, upstream credentials, or request protocol was broken.
actions: Stop making further changes and keep the first failed request.
Check the default logical model, binding priority, channel check, and call records in turn; don't change multiple variables at once.

troubleshooting.symptom: Generation succeeds, but new or historical media can't be displayed
troubleshooting.cause: The media registration, storage_provider, file write, object signing, or in-site media API link is broken.
actions: Test one new media item and one historical media item separately.
Verify the database registration, the real file or object, and the media API response to confirm whether the problem is on write or read.

troubleshooting.symptom: Orders, points balance, plan quota, or refund statistics disagree with each other
troubleshooting.cause: Payment callbacks are delayed or duplicated, failure refunds were missed, manual adjustments went unrecorded, or the statistics use different time ranges.
actions: Build a timeline from a single order or consumption ledger ID.
Compare order, payment, points, and plan ledgers before reversing, and record the reason and responsible person.

troubleshooting.symptom: After deployment or a code update, pages don't change
troubleshooting.cause: An old production build, old container, or old reverse-proxy target is still running; the browser isn't opening the instance you just modified.
actions: Check which host, port, and process start command the accessed domain ultimately proxies to.
Use `npm run dev` in development; in production rebuild, restart, and verify the version information.
